purpose: Nabumetone is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis, including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It helps make it easier to move around and do daily activities. It does not cure arthritis, but it does a great job managing the symptoms.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation. Nabumetone works by blocking enzymes called COX-1 and COX-2 that your body uses to make those pain-causing chemicals. With fewer of those chemicals around, you feel less pain and swelling.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, heartburn, nausea, diarrhea, constipation, gas, dizziness, and headache are the most common side effects. Some people also notice mild swelling in their hands or feet. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medicine can raise your risk of heart attack, stroke, and serious stomach or intestinal bleeding, especially if used for a long time or at high doses. Do not take it if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Talk to your doctor if you have heart disease, kidney or liver problems, high blood pressure, or if you are pregnant. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 1000 mg (one tablet) taken once a day, usually in the evening with food. Your doctor may increase it to 1500 or 2000 mg per day if needed. Always take the lowest dose that works for you, and never take more than prescribed.
